title: What criteria is used to determine if a user had prior given permission for a device | getDevices( )
body:
In the spec description here https://wicg.github.io/webusb/#dom-usb-getdevices

It describes this algorithm to determine if it has seen an allowed device before:

https://wicg.github.io/webusb/#check-permissions-for-device

In practice, I don't see this behavior.  I have a device and we built a USB driver for it and it has been working great.  The user requests pairing once, opts in, and the device operates just fine, even on a page refresh we can still connect to it and find it in `getDevices`.

However, if the device is disconnected (usb cable pulled), and reconnected, when it checks permissions for the device, I would expect it to not have to go through `requestDevice` again, but in this scenario `getDevices` always returns an empty array (after disconnect, followed by reconnect).

This particular device has null/empty serial number in the `USBDevice`, but the vendor and product id obviously didn't change.  On a physical disconnect/reconnect the USB port _might_ change, but I'm trying to figure out why I can't reconnect with it once it has been plugged in and the user opted in prior?  Why is it eliminated from the cache?  Is there some other identifier that could be used to help it not have to go through the whole `requestDevice` pathway?

This has recently become a real problem as the most recent firmware upgrade on these devices now institutes a mandatory 24h power cycle (for regulatory reasons), and thus it gets disconnected and un-paired, which causes the end-user to have to reconnect it every day -- and this has not gone over well.
